title: How Much Fiber in Kidney Beans? 11.3g per Cup
description: Kidney Beans: about 11.3 g of fiber per 1 cup, cooked (40% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in kidney beans?

answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Beans, kidney, all types, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt

intro: Kidney beans rank #7 of 10 beans and legumes on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in kidney beans by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in kidney beans?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists beans, kidney, all types, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt at 6.4 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 cup, cooked; 177 g) therefore has about 11.3 g of fiber and 225 calories. That is 40% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 45% of a 25 g day and 30% of a 38 g day.
Kidney beans are the classic chili and red-beans-and-rice bean. They hold their shape through long simmering, so they work well in big-batch dishes that you portion out over several days.

sections.heading: Cook dried kidney beans thoroughly
paragraphs: Raw or undercooked red kidney beans contain a natural lectin (phytohaemagglutinin) that can cause severe stomach upset. Soak dried beans, then boil them hard for at least 10 minutes before simmering until soft. Slow cookers on low may not get hot enough to do this on their own. Canned kidney beans are already cooked.
USDA’s canned row includes the liquid, which is why it shows less fiber per 100 g than drained cooked beans. If you drain and rinse, the cooked-bean figures are the closer match.

sections.heading: How kidney beans compare with other beans and legumes
paragraphs: Of the 10 beans and legumes on this site, kidney beans rank #7 for fiber per typical serving and #7 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 5 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [chickpeas](/fiber-in-chickpeas) at 12.5 g (1 cup, cooked); [green peas](/fiber-in-green-peas) at 8.8 g (1 cup, cooked); [edamame](/fiber-in-edamame) at 8.1 g (1 cup, shelled, cooked). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), kidney beans are #24 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding kidney beans to your day
paragraphs: One bowl of bean-heavy chili can supply a large share of a day’s fiber. If you make a pot, divide the beans by the number of servings to estimate your bowl.

Example: 1 cup kidney beans, 1 cup white rice, 1 cup green beans. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 15.9 g of fiber, with 11.3 g from the kidney beans. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of kidney beans?
faqs.a: 6.4 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Beans, kidney, all types, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in kidney beans (1/2 cup, cooked)?
faqs.a: About 5.7 g, for 88.5 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in a bowl of chili?
faqs.a: It depends almost entirely on the beans. A bowl with half a cup of kidney beans gets roughly half of 11.3 g from them; tomatoes, onions, and peppers add a little more. Meat adds none.

faqs.q: Are kidney beans safe from the can?
faqs.a: Yes. Canned kidney beans are fully cooked. The cooking warning applies to dried beans you prepare yourself.
